title: Matérn kernel bandits with a known uniform-norm variation budget
summary: The unknown reward functions lie in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space of a public Matérn kernel. Each round reveals one Gaussian-noisy value at the selected point. The objective is to track the current optimal reward. Consecutive functions are compared in the uniform norm, and the variation budget is supplied to the algorithm.

model.instance: The action domain is $[0,1]^d$. The Matern kernel $k=k_{\nu,\ell}$ is public, with smoothness $\nu>0$, length scale $\ell>0$, and $k(x,x)=1$. The environment fixes all reward functions before interaction: $$f_t\in\mathcal H_k,\qquad \|f_t\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\quad(t=1,\ldots,T).$$ $$\sum_{t=2}^{T}\|f_t-f_{t-1}\|_\infty\le V_\infty,\qquad \|g\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in[0,1]^d}|g(x)|.$$

bounds.derivation:
Appendix D.7 of the source handles Gaussian observations by sub-Gaussian truncation. Set the grid error to $1/T$; for fixed Matern kernel parameters, the logarithm of grid size is $O(\log T)$. Choosing failure probability $\delta=T^{-2}$ and using $R_T\le2BT$ yields an expectation bound. Information gain satisfies $\gamma_T=O(T^{d/(2
u+d)}(\log T)^{2
u/(2
u+d)})$. The RKHS-drift variant also uses $k(x,x)\le1$ to derive $\|f-g\|_\infty\le\|f-g\|_{\mathcal H_k}$; the uniform-norm and switching variants require no such norm conversion.
